title: CuTe DSL Data Types for GPU Kernel Development
critical_patterns: Mixed-Precision GEMM: Compute in FP16, accumulate in FP32
Quantization-Aware Operations: INT8 compute with dequantization
Dynamic Precision Selection: Compile-time decision for FP16 or FP32
constraints: Type mismatch in assignments must be explicitly cast
FP16 has limited range and precision
FP64 is slower on consumer GPUs
Tensor core support varies by architecture
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL provides a range of native GPU data types optimized for tensor core operations and numerical precision trade-offs. Key types include various integer and floating-point formats like Int8, Float16, BFloat16, and Float8, each with specific use cases and performance characteristics. Mixed-precision computation is a common pattern, typically using FP16 for compute and FP32 for accumulation, especially in deep learning. The choice of data type should consider precision needs, hardware support, and performance impacts. For instance, Float8 offers high memory bandwidth and compute speed on Hopper+ architectures, while FP16/BF16 are suitable for most deep learning tasks. Integer types like Int8 are used in quantized neural networks, with tensor cores supporting specific integer operations on newer architectures. Developers must handle type conversions explicitly to avoid mismatches and leverage automatic promotion rules for mixed-type operations. Architecture-specific optimizations, such as those for Ampere and Hopper GPUs, influence type selection and performance. Best practices include using the lowest precision that maintains accuracy, matching types to hardware capabilities, and considering memory bandwidth versus precision trade-offs. Debugging type issues involves ensuring correct type assignments and using runtime checks to validate tensor element types. CuTe integrates with frameworks like PyTorch through type mapping and DLPack conversion, facilitating interoperability. Overall, the choice of data type in CuTe DSL is guided by a balance of correctness, hardware compatibility, performance, and memory considerations.
